title: ToolMachineSchema
description: Source of record for the 🛠️tool-machine framework module: tool yields, the tool transaction reducer (open, committed, aborted; keyed upsert in first-insertion order, retract, empty commit = no edit, abort = zero trace), the TransactionRef stamped on every op of a committed transaction, the refusals and abort reasons, the runner step (including host abort, reset and persist/resume) and the transaction-law fixture with its example drag gesture charts. Wire names are camelCase except the hybrid logical timestamp, which keeps the replication wire names; u64 values are JSON integers.

TransactionId.description: `tx-` + the first 8 bytes of blake3(write_str(actor) | varint(hlc.actor) | varint(hlc.physical_ms) | varint(hlc.logical) | write_str(tool)) as lowercase hex; write_str = varint byte length + UTF-8, varint = unsigned LEB128.

TransactionRef.title: TransactionRef
TransactionRef.description: The committed tool transaction that authored an operation (replication `TransactionRef`).

ToolYield.title: ToolYield
ToolYield.description: One effect of a tool machine. `mutation` is the tool's parametric mutation, opaque to the transaction.

ToolRefusal.description: toolTransaction.closed: a yield reached a committed or aborted transaction, or arrived while entering the initial configuration. toolTransaction.unclosed: an event left the tool at rest (its root's initial state active) with the transaction open. Every refusal publishes nothing and drops the transaction.

ToolAbortReason.description: Who ended a transaction without an edit: the tool's abort yield, or a host cancel.

TransactionEntries.description: Provisional entries in first-insertion order; keys are unique.

ToolStep.title: ToolStep
ToolStep.description: What one event or host cancel did to a runner's transaction slot. `open` carries the runner's open transaction (ref and provisional entries); `committed` the batch to publish as exactly one edit; `aborted` (with who aborted) and `empty` publish nothing.

GestureInput.title: GestureInput
GestureInput.description: Example drag gesture input: a magnet the dragged pointer connects to within `radius` (inclusive, Euclidean).

GestureMutation.title: GestureMutation
GestureMutation.description: Example parametric mutations: the net drag offset and a connection to the magnet.

GestureAction.description: press: remember the origin. drag: upsert `translate` {dx, dy} from the origin (retract it at zero offset), then upsert `connect` to the magnet when the pointer is within the radius, else retract it. release: commit. cancel: abort.

GestureChart.title: GestureChart
GestureChart.description: The example tool statechart; the Rust `statechart!`, the TS kernel tables and the xstate oracle are all built to this chart.

oneOf.description: An event that settled into a step.
A host abort and the step it reported.
A silent host reset and the transaction it dropped.
The host persists the runner (`into_parts`) and resumes it with a fresh host; nothing is reported and the gesture continues.

refused.description: Indices of the yields the closed transaction refused.

resume.description: Resume admission over the drag chart: a snapshot in `state` (reached by driving the chart) with no, an open, a committed or an aborted transaction; `ok` or the refusal.

ScrubGesture.description: The press a continuous control's dispatch belongs to (`<control key>:<ms>`); non-empty.

ScrubPhase.title: ScrubPhase
ScrubPhase.description: Where one dispatch of a continuous control sits in its press: a live tick, the release, or a host cancel (its dispatch carries no value).

ScrubArgs.description: The scrub protocol arguments a continuous control merges into its binding's args (`value` rides beside them).

ScrubInput.title: ScrubInput
ScrubInput.description: What reaches a scrub: a tick's or the release's ABSOLUTE leaves (the plugin's leaf constructor applied to the value), or a host cancel.

ScrubOpen.title: ScrubOpen
ScrubOpen.description: One window's open scrub as the ledger persists it (window transient, never history): the press, the document revision it opened on, the authoring tool, the open transaction and its keyed leaves (`0`, `1`, … of the latest tick).

ScrubStep.title: ScrubStep
ScrubStep.description: What one scrub input did: `open` names the transaction the press holds; the other kinds are the runner's `ToolStep`s.

oneOf.description: One input of a window's press.
A host cancel of one window's press (only of `gesture` when named).
A host cancel of every open press (time-travel freeze).
The window roster: every other window's press retires.

ScrubChart.title: ScrubChart
ScrubChart.description: The scrub statechart; the Rust tables, the `statechart!` reference compilation, the TS tables and the xstate oracle are all this chart.

fingerprint.description: The `statechart!` fingerprint (u64, decimal) gating a persisted scrub's restore.

ScrubLawFixture.title: ScrubLawFixture
ScrubLawFixture.description: Language-agnostic laws of the scrub machine and ledger (`🧫️fixtures/🧫️scrub-law`): argument parsing, the chart, and step-by-step scenarios with independently minted transaction ids.

TypingBuffer.description: The text buffer a live typing delivery types into (its editor surface id); non-empty.

TypingCommit.title: TypingCommit
TypingCommit.description: Why a typing run ended as ONE edit: the author paused, the caret jumped away, the editor lost focus, Enter in a single-line field, the page was hidden or left, an explicit apply, or another verb needs the typed text first.

TypingPhase.title: TypingPhase
TypingPhase.description: Where one dispatch sits in its buffer`s typing run: a typed edit, or the host`s commit signal (no edit).

TypingArgs.description: The typing protocol arguments a live text editor merges into its typing verb`s args.

TypingInput.title: TypingInput
TypingInput.description: What reaches a typing run: one typed edit`s leaves, a commit, or a host abort (a conflicting base, a frozen document).

TypingFold.title: TypingFold
TypingFold.description: How the leaves of one typed edit join the open run: the run`s new net leaves, or a split (the open run commits as it is, the edit opens the next).

TypingOpen.title: TypingOpen
TypingOpen.description: One window`s open typing run as the ledger persists it (window transient, never history): its buffer, the authoring tool, the idle deadline, the open transaction and its keyed net leaves.

oneOf.description: One typed edit of a window`s run.
A host commit signal of one window`s run.
A host abort of one window`s run.
The idle lapse at a clock: every run whose deadline it reached commits.
A host abort of every run (a frozen document).
Another verb: every run commits first.
The window roster: every other window`s run commits like a blur.

TypingChart.title: TypingChart
TypingChart.description: The typing statechart; the Rust tables, the `statechart!` reference compilation, the TS tables and the xstate oracle are all this chart.

fingerprint.description: The `statechart!` fingerprint (u64, decimal) gating a persisted run`s restore.

TypingLawFixture.title: TypingLawFixture
TypingLawFixture.description: Language-agnostic laws of the typing machine and ledger (`🧫️fixtures/🧫️typing-law`): argument parsing, the chart, the fixture`s typing algebra, and step-by-step scenarios with independently minted transaction ids.

NodeDragRow.title: NodeDragRow
NodeDragRow.description: The node-graph gesture record (design §13.3): the ONE `nodeGraphEdit` row every node-graph host dispatches for a released node drag — the press it closes, each moved node once, and the ONE offset every node moved by, relative to where it started. Rust `NodeDragRecord::from_row`, TypeScript `nodeDragRecordFromRow`.

NodeDragLawFixture.title: NodeDragLawFixture
NodeDragLawFixture.description: `🧫️fixtures/🧫️node-drag-law/🔣️.json`: valid rows with their decoded record and `moves`, invalid rows with the reason, and one one-shot commit of the node-drag machine.
